problem: Express $\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+6)}+\frac{C}{(x+5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+6$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)$ and get

$$
3{x}^{2}+2x-3=(Ax+B)(x+5)+C({x}^{2}+6).
$$

Plugging in $x=-5$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(-5)^{2}+2(-5)-3 & =(A(-5)+B)(-5+5)+C((-5)^{2}+6) \\ 75-10-3 & =31C \\ C & =\frac{62}{31} \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(0)^{2}+2(0)-3 & =(A(0)+B)(0+5)+C((0)^{2}+6) \\ -3 & =5B+6C \\ -3 & =5B+6(2) \\ 5B & =-3-12 \\ B & =\frac{-15}{5} \\ B & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A$ we choose $x=1$, and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}+2(1)-3 & =(A(1)+B)(1+5)+C((1)^{2}+6) \\ 2 & =6A+6B+7C \\ 2 & =6A+6(-3)+7(2) \\ 6A & =2+18-14 \\ A & =\frac{6}{6} \\ A & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=1,B=-3,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}+2x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)(x+5)}=\frac{x-3}{({x}^{2}+6)}+\frac{2}{(x+5)}.
$$
